label: OptiXtrans E9605 OTN line shelf, 5x TNG1N210 (50x 10G line)
description: Huawei OptiXtrans E9605 - 177 mm (4U) metro/access OTN line shelf with 5 service-board slots and no electrical cross-connect (the vendor table prints Cross-connect Type: NA, so the shelf relays line boards rather than grooming them). Modelled fully populated with 5x TNG1N210 line boards: 50x 10G WDM-side line ports, each carrying one OTU2 or OTU2e wavelength.
notes:
Stated card complement, not a fixed chassis figure: the E9605 has 5 service slots, so "5x TNG1N210" is what 50 line ports means. A partly filled shelf, or the same shelf with TNG1N206 (6x 10G) or TNG1N401 (1x 100G) in place of the N210, is a different box - model it separately rather than reusing this one. Same convention as devices/huawei/optixtrans-e6616.json.

Frame, from the cited product page (read 2026-11-18, HTTP 200, 344,532 B): 442 x 295 x 177 mm, Number of Service Slots 5, Cross-connect Type NA, 120 wavelengths at 50 GHz in C and L band, line rates 10G to 1.2T, service types SDH/SONET/PDH/Ethernet/SAN/OTN/Video. Huawei board documentation places a single-slot board in IU1-IU5 of an E9605 subrack (TNG2DAP section 1.9, Valid Slots table, e-file PDF read 2026-11-17: https://e-file.huawei.com/marketingcloud/pep/asset/20000001/Material/e75c775ac71144e6b522d7cef1601604/M3T1A669N1188254864652623965/TNG2DAP%20-.pdf).

Board validity and port count come from the OptiXtrans E9600 (E9624/E9612/E9605) Boards Overview chapter, tables 1 and 3: the N206/N210 row reads Y in the E9605 subrack column, and the board is named "TNG1N210: 10 x 10 Gbit/s Line Service Processing Board". That chapter is EDOC1100126589BEJ09047, which is behind the support wall - the vendor copy (OptiXtrans E9600 Board Datasheet, EDOC1100163901) answers 302 -> /view/notFound for every user-agent tried - so it was read from the verbatim partner copy at https://www.actfornet.com/solutions/solution/OptiXtrans_E9600_Boards_Overview (HTTP 200, 226,637 B, 2026-11-18), whose 127 support.huawei.com/hedex topic links identify the chapter. The fields above are recorded from that chapter text; they were not invented, and the cage/rate they name is the board name itself, not an inference from a sibling frame.

Line side is OTU2/OTU2e over DWDM, not Ethernet. The engine has no OTN type, so the ports are filed as ethernet/sfp+ - the physical cage - and the protocol claim is written down here instead. The link validator will therefore accept a 10GBASE-LR peer on a port that only carries OTU2: that is the house convention, shared by devices/huawei/optixtrans-e6616.json, devices/ciena/waveserver-ai.json, devices/adva/fsp-3000.json and devices/packetlight/pl-2000m.json, all of which pass scripts/audit-port-types.js. A real otn/wdm type is an engine change and would fix it for all five.

No fabric block: the E9605 has no cross-connect to declare (vendor table: Cross-connect Type NA), and the N210 terminates 10 OTU2 wavelengths per board rather than switching client traffic - so there is no L2/L3 forwarding and capabilities is cli only. No PoE.
